---
title: Storage Cost Comparison
---

These estimates compare US list prices and monthly storage charges in US dollars.
AWS rates use US East (N. Virginia), and consumer plans use US pricing. The
estimates exclude API requests, retrieval, egress, temporary restore copies, tax,
and discounts. The 1 TB comparison uses 1,000 GB.

## 100 GB

**Prices as of 1 August 2026.**

| Service | Monthly cost | Price used | Supported by this CLI |
|---|---:|---|:---:|
| AWS S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval | **$0.40** | $0.004/GB-month | Yes |
| AWS S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval | **$0.36** | $0.0036/GB-month | Yes; restore required |
| AWS S3 Standard | **$2.30** | $0.023/GB-month | Yes |
| Backblaze B2 | **$0.63** | $0.00695/GB-month after the first 10 GB free | Yes |
| Google Drive | **$1.99** | Google One Basic 100 GB plan | No |
| OneDrive | **$1.99** | Microsoft 365 Basic 100 GB plan | No |

## Cost of listing files in a snapshot

Restic can list a snapshot without downloading the backed-up file contents:

```sh
uv run restic-backups generic restic run --backup <job-id> ls <snapshot-id>
```

The command downloads repository indexes, snapshot records, directory trees,
and other required metadata. Commands such as `restore` and `dump` download file
data. Restic's local cache can reduce metadata reads on subsequent commands.
Set `cache-dir` on a `restic-repositories` entry to give each repository a
stable, separate cache location; see [Configuration](configuration.qmd).

Prime that cache with repository metadata before browsing snapshots:

```sh
uv run restic-backups generic repository prime-cache <repository-id>
```

This runs `restic check --with-cache`; it does not download backed-up file data.

| Provider | Metadata-read charges | Typical cost |
|---|---|---:|
| Backblaze B2 | GET and LIST transactions are free; egress is free up to 3× average monthly storage | **$0** within the free egress allowance |
| AWS S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval, US East | $0.03/GB retrieved plus about $0.01 per 1,000 GET requests | Usually **less than $0.01** |

Glacier Instant Retrieval examples below show retrieval charges only; request
charges are additional:

| Metadata downloaded | Retrieval charge |
|---:|---:|
| 10 MB | ~$0.0003 |
| 100 MB | ~$0.003 |
| 1 GB | $0.03 |

AWS currently includes the first 100 GB per month of internet data transfer out,
aggregated across AWS services and regions. Backblaze charges $0.01/GB only for
egress beyond its free allowance. Exact costs depend on the repository's
metadata size, object count, local cache, and other usage during the billing
month.

## Important differences

AWS and Backblaze prices are metered object-storage charges. Google Drive and
OneDrive prices are fixed consumer subscription tiers that include other
services. This project supports S3-compatible and local filesystem storage;
Google Drive and OneDrive cannot be selected as storage backends.

Both Glacier classes have a 90-day minimum storage duration. Instant Retrieval
is immediately readable but has a 128 KB minimum billable object size and
separate data-retrieval charges. Flexible Retrieval first requires an archive
restore: expedited retrieval typically takes 1–5 minutes, standard takes 3–5
hours, and bulk takes 5–12 hours. It also bills 40 KB of metadata per object,
which is not included in the estimates above.

For Flexible Retrieval, configure a `restore` policy and set
`ALLOW_ARCHIVE_RETRIEVAL=1` when running retrieval-related commands. S3 Standard
and B2 do not require an archive restore before normal access. Backblaze includes
free egress up to three times average monthly storage; AWS transfer and request
charges vary by usage and region.

Prices vary by country and can change. Check the current official pages before
choosing a provider:

- [Amazon S3 pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/s3/pricing/)
- [AWS archive retrieval options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/restoring-objects-retrieval-options.html)
- [Backblaze B2 pricing](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/pricing)
- [Backblaze B2 transaction pricing](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/transaction-pricing)
- [Google One plans](https://one.google.com/about/plans?hl=en_US)
- [Microsoft OneDrive plans](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/onedrive/onedrive-plans-and-pricing?market=us)
